readings.reading: the brain, its cells and the ear

body.note: nine units read as seven chambers and two openings, the walled center, the veins as the links, the castles as Schloss, the suns as heat, fluid, labels; the outward towers, the T-O map, the stars and the wheels unexplained
body.who: Keagan Brewer and Michelle L. Lewis, Social History of Medicine, 2024
body.must_be_true: a seven-celled womb in the period's books
body.found: true: the seven-celled womb is a medieval teaching (the Salernitan and later gynaecological texts), as Brewer and Lewis cite

body.reading: cells of tissue, as a lens shows them
body.note: a walled center and fields of small round bodies, linked; no towers, suns, T-O map or labels
body.must_be_true: a lens strong enough to show cells before 1438
body.found: not found: spectacles (Pisa, about 1286) and reading stones magnify a few times (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glasses; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reading_stone); the compound microscope dates from the 1590s and cells were first seen in 1665 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microscope)

body.reading: the organs of the bathing pages
body.note: tubes and fluid between organs, labelled; the foldout's circles, towers and heavens unexplained
body.who: voynich.nu illustration descriptions; Davis 2015 (f77v as a uterus)
body.must_be_true: the tubes and pools drawn as organs
body.found: open: the drawings' study reads them as pools and pipes; an organ reading rests on their shapes alone

body.note: a nebula's stars and a spiral; nothing else
body.found: not found: neither instrument existed before about 1600 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microscope); Manly refuted Newbold's cipher in 1931

body.reading: the brain's cells, the medieval ventricles
body.note: the ventricles are three to five cells in a row joined by passages, labelled; not nine round units in a grid, and nothing in them is a tower, sun, star or map
body.must_be_true: the cells drawn as chambers in a head, known before 1438
body.found: true: the ventricle theory and its diagrams in a head run from late antiquity through the 1400s; Mondino de Luzzi described the brain from dissection in 1316 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mondino_de_Luzzi)

body.note: a walled center and wavy folds; nothing else
body.must_be_true: a drawing of the brain's surface before 1438
body.found: not found: the brain's folds were drawn as such only from the 1500s on; period diagrams draw cells, not folds

body.reading: the ear and how hearing works
body.note: tubes and fluid; the cochlea's spiral appears nowhere on the foldout, which has wheels of petals, not spirals
body.must_be_true: a picture of the ear's inner parts before 1438
body.found: partly: Avicenna's Canon describes the outer ear, the drum and a winding inner passage in words; the ossicles were first described in the 1500s, and no drawing of the inner ear before 1500 was found
